If you agree with the statements below, and you want to take part in the experiment, click 'Continue'.
If you do not agree, you can click 'Exit' and leave the room. 


"I have read and I understand the information provided about this study."

"I have had the opportunity to ask questions, and those questions have been sufficiently answered."

"I understand that my data will not have identifying information on it, so people will not know my name or which data belongs to me."

"You can use my coded data for scientific research and share these data, either directly with other researchers or in a public online repository."

name: text
value:
To participate in this study, you should be healthy and have no current psychiatric, neurological or psychological disorders. You should be able to focus on a computer game for around 30 minutes.

Participating in this study is harmless. The only downside of participation is your time investment.

At the beginning of the session, you will be given instructions and some examples of the task. You will then perform the visual decision-making task. Once you complete the task, you will be fully debriefed and receive your compensation.

name: text
value:
Participation in this study is completely voluntary. This means that you can stop at any time, without explanation, and without consequences for you.

If you decide to end your participation before the experiment has been completed, you will be compensated for the time that you have spent up to that point (rounded to the nearest 15 minutes, by means of 1 credit per half an hour).

All information you provide will be treated as strictly private.
Your data will be processed and stored in a coded way, by assigning it a unique code rather than your name. 
The data you provide will be used for scientific research. We may share these coded data with other researchers, or via publicly accessible online repositories. 
If you do not agree to make your coded research data publicly accessible, you cannot participate in this study.

name: text
value:
On each trial, you must decide which of the two target images has the higher contrast (i.e., appears darker). 
To select the target with the higher contrast, simply move the mouse until the chosen target reaches the center of the screen.

For example, in the image below, the right target has the higher contrast, so you would move your mouse to the left.

Click 'Continue' to see more instructions and another example.

name: text
value:
In this example image, the left target has the higher contrast, so you would move your mouse to the right.

To interact with the game, you will only need to move the mouse; clicking does not do anything.

Click 'Continue' to see more instructions.

name: text
value:
You will hear a high beep if you answer correctly.
If you answer incorrectly, you will hear a buzzing noise instead.
If you take too long to answer, you will hear a low beep.

Please try to be as accurate and fast as possible, and try not to let the trial time-out without a response.


Click 'Continue' to practice a few example trials.

name: text
value:
That is the end of the practice trials.

Here is a last reminder of the instructions:

In each trial, you will hear a beep and two targets will appear.
You must decide which target has the higher contrast.
To respond, move your mouse left or right to bring the chosen target into the middle of the screen. You don't need to click, simply drag the mouse.

If you are correct, you will hear a high beep; if you are incorrect, you will hear a buzzing noise.

Important: durig the game you will see a red cross i the middle of the screen. Please try to keep your eyes fixated on this cross throughout the experiment.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask out loud, the experimenter can hear you and will help you out.

You will now start the real experiment. Good luck!

name: text
value:
That's the end of the task.

Thank you for participating! Now that you are done, we can tell you a bit more about the experiment.


In this project, we want to study how well people integrate past information into their decisions. 

You just participated in a decision-making task modelled after a similar task designed by the International Brain Laboratory consortium.

Click 'Continue' to read more.

name: text
value:
When the visual stimulus was ambiguous, you should then have biased your responses toward the location with more frequent targets in the recent past. 

For example, if 3 out of 4 previous images were shown on the right, an expectation ("I think the next image will appear on the right") should guide your decisions ("I'm not sure, so let's choose right"). 

The more probable image location could change unexpectedly, so you should have continually tracked the statistics of the task and updated your expectations accordingly.

name: text
value:
You watched a pair of stimuli on the screen, and judged the location of the more visible stimulus, which varied in difficulty. 

To invite you to combine this visual information with your expectations about the most likely location, we varied the probability of whether the target stimulus would appear on the left or right side.

name: text
value:
If you have any questions or concerns about the experiment or your data, please let the experimenter know.

If you are participating for SONA credits, you will receive your credits before the end of the day.

If you are participating for money, you should receive compensation in approximately 2 weeks. Once you have closed the experiment, you can fill in your payment information in the other room.

Click 'Finish' to save your data and exit the experiment.

Thank you! We will now move on to the experiment.

You will take part in a computer game.
However, you will not receive any instructions: the goal is to figure out the rules of the game by yourself.

To interact with the game, you will only need to move the mouse; clicking does not do anything.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask out loud, The experimenter can hear you and will help you out.

When you are ready, click 'Start experiment'.
